coverage.note: gap and hole not separable in my rule; availability by month 57% (Oct) to 97% (Jul); by logged km: <=2 87%, 2-10 82%, >10 74%

verdict_wording: E_int rel +1.17% [1.03, 1.39]: NOT consistent within +-1% (interval above 1%), consistent within +-3%; median|diff| 0.11 km <= 0.25 km. Wording: 'difference of +1.2% [1.0, 1.4], cloud larger'; small bias, direction stated. Not 'accurate'.
rules_inferred: Local-time start to UTC via Europe/Kyiv; end = start + duration_s
Rows at the 2 conflict timestamps dropped (conflicts rows keyed by timestamp, both fields)
Flat bracket: |dV|<=0.05 gives exact endpoint any gap; otherwise gap<=35 s
E_br availability = same bracket test as E_int, value = first row >= t1 minus last row <= t0
Jump check on consecutive rows within [t0-35,t1+35]; positive step with dt<=0 counted as jump
Shift16: both endpoints queried at t-16 s
Anchor: only the after-last-row fraction of a straddling drive added (none straddled; 4 whole drives)
concerns: Positive E_int difference contradicts spec 9.1 expectation (negative from parked edges): the +1.2% is not an edge artefact; E_int and E_br differ by only 0.05 pp
Availability is selected by month and decreasing with drive length (74% for >10 km, 57% in Oct): a long-drive/month selection effect on the aggregate is not excluded
Shift16 raises n to 432 (more brackets inside cap), so the sensitivity changes the sample, not only the offset
Aggregate rests on 420 drives dominated by long ones; shared wheel-speed scale caveat applies
